text:
Before registering, you should check if you need to register for the Economic Crime Levy.

When to register

You must register before you submit a return for the Economic Crime Levy as soon as you can, this is because payments for the levy are due by 30 September of every year.

What you will need

You’ll need to tell us:

information about your UK revenue for the last financial year

the date when your organisation started anti-money laundering-regulated activities, if you started in the past financial year

the business sector your organisation operates in

information about the length of your accounting period

You’ll also need to tell us the contact details of someone in your organisation, including their:

name

role

email address

telephone number

If you are a general partnership or a Scottish partnership

You’ll also need to tell us:

your partnership Unique Tax Reference

the postcode you use for Self Assessment

If you are a limited company

You’ll also need to tell us your:

company registration number

Corporation Tax Unique Tax Reference

If you are a limited liability partnership or a limited partnership

You’ll also need to tell us:

your partnership company registration number

your partnership Unique Tax Reference

the postcode you use for Self Assessment

If you are an unlimited company or a Scottish limited partnership

You’ll also need to tell us your:

company registration number

Corporation Tax Unique Tax Reference

If you are a sole trader

You’ll also need to tell us your:

National Insurance number

Unique Tax Reference

If you are a charity

You’ll also need to tell us your:

charity registration number

company registration number

business name

If you are a trust

You’ll also need to tell us your:

Corporation Tax Unique Tax Reference

company name

If you are an unincorporated association

You’ll also need to tell us your:

Corporation Tax Unique Tax Reference — if you have one

company name

postcode

If you are a registered society

You’ll also need to tell us your:

company registration number

registered society Unique Tax Reference

If you are a non-UK establishment

You’ll also need to tell us your:

Self Assessment Unique Tax Reference

Corporation Tax Unique Tax Reference

company name

company registration number — if you have one

How to register

You must use the online service to register for the Economic Crime Levy if you are supervised by HMRC or one of the professional bodies.

To register, you’ll need the sign in details of the person or entity who is completing the registration.

If you do not already have sign in details, you’ll be able to create them when you sign in for the first time.

If you are registering more than one entity, you’ll need to create a separate sign in for each one.

Register now

Online services may be slow during busy times. Check if there are any problems with this service.

If you experience technical issues with this service, select the ‘Is this page not working properly?’ link on the page where you need help.

After you have registered

You will receive an Economic Crime Levy registration number. You will need to keep it for your records because every year you will need to submit a return for the Economic Crime Levy.

If you need to amend your registration

You can change your registration if:

the original information you gave us is wrong

your circumstances have changed

To amend your registration, sign in to your Economic Crime Levy account.

Contact HMRC for help with Economic Crime Levy

Only call HMRC for help with Economic Crime Levy if you cannot find an answer using our online services or guidance.

This helpline may ask you some security questions.

Make sure your details are up to date in your Economic Crime Levy account or you could fail telephone security.

If you have already registered, you will need your Economic Crime Levy registration number. You can find this:

in your Economic Crime Levy account

in your HMRC business tax account if you have one

on the confirmation email HMRC sent you to confirm your Economic Crime Levy return had been submitted

Telephone: 0300 322 9621

Opening times: Monday to Friday, 10am to 4pm. Closed bank holidays.

Find out about call charges.
